question: In trials of ulcer treatments, which worked better as a placebo?
answer: Four. Goldacre describes a review of ulcer trials in which four placebo pills a day healed more ulcers than two. Colour, price and form matter too: injections beat pills, and branded fake pills beat plain ones. What a treatment looks like changes how much it seems to work.
move: How a treatment is presented can change how well it seems to work.
trap: 'They worked the same': a sugar pill is a sugar pill.
simply: Your body can feel better just because it expects to. More pills, or a fancy box, make the expectation bigger, so even fake pills 'work' more.
why: It is why any treatment needs a fair comparison with a placebo before you believe it, and why expensive packaging is not evidence.

book.title: Bad Science
book.author: Ben Goldacre
book.badge: By an NHS doctor and Guardian columnist

reference: Ben Goldacre, Bad Science (Fourth Estate, 2008), ch. 5
